questions.stem: Which of the following is a fixed cost for a bakery?

options.text: The flour used to bake bread
The annual rent paid on the bakery premises
Electricity consumed by the ovens
Wages paid to casual loaders per delivery

questions.explanation: Rent must be paid in full whether the bakery produces one loaf or ten thousand, so it does not vary with output. That independence from output is the test of a fixed cost.

distractorRationale.a: Flour is consumed in proportion to loaves baked, so it is a variable cost
distractorRationale.c: Oven electricity rises with the number of baking cycles
distractorRationale.d: Payment per delivery varies directly with the quantity dispatched

questions.stem: A firm's total cost is ₦520 when output is 4 units and ₦650 when output is 5 units. What is the marginal cost of the fifth unit, in naira? Give a number only.
questions.explanation: Marginal cost is the change in total cost caused by the extra unit: ₦650 − ₦520 = ₦130. Dividing total cost by output would instead give average total cost, which is ₦130 here only by coincidence of these figures.

questions.stem: A firm maximises profit at the level of output where

options.text: total revenue is at its highest
marginal cost equals marginal revenue
average total cost is at its lowest
total cost equals total revenue

questions.explanation: While marginal revenue exceeds marginal cost, each extra unit adds more to revenue than to cost and raises profit; once marginal cost exceeds marginal revenue, extra units reduce profit. Profit is therefore greatest where the two are equal with marginal cost rising.

distractorRationale.a: Maximum revenue ignores cost entirely, and is usually reached at a larger output than maximum profit
distractorRationale.c: Minimum average cost gives the most efficient scale, but not necessarily the most profitable output
distractorRationale.d: Where total cost equals total revenue the firm breaks even and profit is zero

questions.stem: Average fixed cost falls continuously as output increases because

options.text: total fixed cost falls as output increases
the same total fixed cost is spread over a larger number of units
variable cost per unit falls as output increases
marginal cost falls as output increases

questions.explanation: Total fixed cost stays constant, so dividing it by an ever larger output must give a smaller figure per unit. A ₦200 rent is ₦200 per unit at one unit but ₦40 per unit at five units.

distractorRationale.a: Total fixed cost by definition does not change with output
distractorRationale.c: Average variable cost typically falls then rises, so it cannot explain a continuous fall
distractorRationale.d: Marginal cost eventually rises because of diminishing returns

questions.stem: A farmer on one hectare records total product of 10, 24, 39, 52, 60, 60 and 54 bags as workers are added one at a time. Diminishing returns set in from the

options.text: third worker
fourth worker
sixth worker
seventh worker

questions.explanation: Marginal products are 10, 14, 15, 13, 8, 0 and −6. The peak is 15 at the third worker, so the first fall occurs with the fourth worker, whose marginal product is 13. Diminishing returns begin where marginal product starts to fall, not where total product starts to fall.

distractorRationale.a: The third worker's marginal product of 15 is the highest, so returns are still increasing
distractorRationale.c: At the sixth worker marginal product reaches zero and total product peaks, which is much later than the onset of diminishing returns
distractorRationale.d: At the seventh worker marginal product is negative, so total product is actually falling

questions.stem: For a firm that can sell any quantity at the ruling market price,

options.text: average revenue equals marginal revenue equals price
marginal revenue lies below average revenue
average revenue falls as output rises
total revenue is constant at every level of output

questions.explanation: A price taker does not have to lower its price to sell more, so each extra unit brings in exactly the ruling price. Average and marginal revenue therefore coincide with price and the revenue curve is a horizontal line.

distractorRationale.b: Marginal revenue lies below average revenue only for a price maker such as a monopolist
distractorRationale.c: A falling average revenue implies the firm must cut price to sell more, which contradicts price taking
distractorRationale.d: Total revenue rises steadily, since it is price multiplied by a growing quantity

questions.stem: A price-taking firm sells at ₦150 per unit. Its total cost is ₦650 at an output of 5 units. What is its profit at that output, in naira? Give a number only.
questions.explanation: Total revenue is ₦150 × 5 = ₦750, and total cost is ₦650, so profit is ₦750 − ₦650 = ₦100. Checking neighbouring outputs shows this is the maximum, since the sixth unit would cost ₦210 to produce but earn only ₦150.

questions.stem: Marginal product equals average product at the output where average product is at its maximum.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. While marginal product is above average product it pulls the average up, and while it is below it drags the average down, so the two must be equal precisely at the peak of average product. In the schedule used in the lesson both equal 13 bags at the fourth worker.

distractorRationale.b: This overlooks the arithmetic relationship between a marginal value and the average it is changing
